rationale:
The shared prune-floor refusal sentence ends with a fixed clause that is FALSE for three of its four consumers, and it was observed telling a real operator something untrue in production on 2026-08-02.

The sentence, built in prune_floor.go's Reason(): "NOTHING was deleted; the rows this run did not confirm are retained and a later run that sees the whole corpus will prune them. If the shrinkage is genuine, re-run with prune_floor_ratio lowered."

That second clause describes ONE consumer's behaviour. index_code_symbols (bugs_closed/135) skips only the PRUNE — its own writes stand, the unconfirmed rows are kept, and a later full run genuinely does tidy them. The other three consumers (save_page_sections, populate_nav_tables, extract_and_sync_links) refuse the WHOLE operation, because delete and insert are one transaction and refusing half would double every row. For them nothing is written, nothing is tidied later, and the artefact already stored still stands. The operator is told to wait for a clean-up that will never come.

This was filed as reasoning when sites B and C were built. It is now a production artefact: the bugs_open/165 site B induction on oufe.com (2026-08-02 10:24 BST, correlation 323173dd-9fd1-4899-bb61-f835f0516b13) produced exactly this sentence in orchestration_states.error, on a refusal where nothing was retained pending anything.

The fix makes the clause a REQUIRED caller-supplied parameter rather than an optional one with a default. That is deliberate and it is the whole design: the failure mode here is not a caller who forgets, it is a default that is silently wrong. A required parameter makes it impossible for a fifth consumer to inherit somebody else's aftermath by saying nothing — the compiler asks the question. An empty string degrades to the SHORTER sentence ("NOTHING was deleted.") rather than to any consumer's clause, because that shorter sentence is true for every possible consumer and a borrowed one is not.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT CHANGE: the decision rule. evaluatePruneFloor, the cohort arithmetic, the floor resolution, the fail-closed behaviour and every consumer's refuse/allow outcome are untouched. Only the human sentence changes. Per the owner ruling of 2026-07-29 (CLAUDE.md, three answers), an addition to a shared mechanism needs an RFC only when it changes what that mechanism GUARANTEES; this changes what it SAYS, and the guarantee is identical. It is therefore submitted to the normal gate.

OTHER CONSUMERS, NAMED AND TOLD (2026-07-29 ruling item 3): all four call sites are updated in this same commit, so no consumer is left on a stale signature — the change is compile-enforced, not advisory. code_symbols_actions.go belongs to bugs_closed/135 (closed); nav_prune_floor.go and link_registry_prune_floor.go were written by the contributing lane on bugs_open/165 and this lane owns that case. The thing those owners need to know is not the new parameter but the guarantee change: their consumers' refusal text now says what THEY do, not what 135 does. Recorded in bugs_open/165.

plan.summary: Make the prune-floor refusal's 'what happens next' clause a required caller-supplied parameter, so each of the four consumers states its own aftermath instead of inheriting the code-index consumer's, which is false for three of them.

edits.rationale: The borrowed clause is the defect. Making aftermath a required parameter closes the door rather than documenting it: a fifth consumer cannot silently inherit a wrong sentence, because there is nothing to inherit. Empty degrades to the shorter, universally-true sentence rather than to a default, so silence is safe instead of silently wrong.

edits.rationale: Two new tests, plus the nine existing call sites updated. The NEGATIVE assertion is the load-bearing half of the first: asserting only that the caller's clause appears would still pass if the borrowed sentence were appended alongside it. Both were proven by mutation from a fresh baseline — restoring the fixed borrowed clause fails both tests; making the empty case fall back to a consumer's clause fails exactly the second. Restore verified and the full package re-run green.

grounded_in: THE DEFECT, as shipped: prune_floor.go Reason() default branch — "NOTHING was deleted; the rows this run did not confirm are retained and a later run that sees the whole corpus will prune them." A fixed clause, identical for all four consumers.

THE FALSE CASE, live in production 2026-08-02 10:24 BST. orchestration_states.error for correlation 323173dd-9fd1-4899-bb61-f835f0516b13: "step refresh_nav_tables failed: ... populate_nav_tables: rebuild: REFUSED for site oufe.com — this run re-confirmed too little of what is stored (prune_floor_ratio=0.50): nav items 33% (8 of 24). NOTHING was deleted; the rows this run did not confirm are retained and a later run that sees the whole corpus will prune them." Nothing was retained pending a later prune: the whole rebuild was refused.

WHY THE THREE DIFFER FROM THE ONE, from nav_prune_floor.go's own header: "WHY THE REFUSAL FAILS THE WHOLE ACTION, like site A and unlike 135. The delete and the insert are one operation inside one transaction: refusing the delete but performing the insert would double every nav item. So the action returns an error before opening the transaction, leaving the existing good nav in place."

THE CONSUMER COUNT IS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED: grep -rn '\.Reason(' platform/ internal/ pkg/ --include=*.go excluding tests returns exactly four call sites — code_symbols_actions.go:346, save_sections_prune_floor.go:211, nav_prune_floor.go:209, link_registry_prune_floor.go:168. All four are updated here, so the change is compile-enforced and no consumer can be left on a stale signature.

THE GUARANTEE IS UNCHANGED: evaluatePruneFloor, pruneCohort.ratio, the floor clamping, the Stored=0 first-appearance rule and every allow/refuse outcome are untouched by this diff. Only the human sentence in the refused branch changes, plus the signature that feeds it.

MUTATION EVIDENCE, run rather than claimed, fresh baseline each time (the 2026-07-31 lesson: a wrong restore path makes mutations accumulate and every one 'fails as expected'). M1 restoring the fixed borrowed clause: both new tests FAIL, the first naming the exact forbidden string. M2 making an empty aftermath fall back to 135's clause: exactly TestRefusalWithNoAftermathDegradesToATrueSentence FAILS. Restore verified by grep count, full package green after.
plan.risks:
SIGNATURE CHANGE ACROSS FOUR CONSUMERS, two of them other lanes' files. Mitigated by it being compile-enforced — a missed call site cannot build, so there is no silent-drift failure mode. All four are in this one commit, and the tree was verified clean for every one of them immediately before editing (git status --porcelain on each path returned nothing).

REQUIRED RATHER THAN OPTIONAL PARAMETER is a deliberate ergonomic cost. An optional variant (a second method, or a default) would be less intrusive and would reintroduce exactly the defect: a consumer that says nothing gets somebody else's aftermath. Ranked by what makes the bad state unrepresentable rather than by what is smallest.

THE EMPTY-STRING PATH still exists and is reachable. It is bounded to a strictly-true shorter sentence and pinned by its own test including the dangling-separator case, but a caller passing "" does lose the 'what happens next' guidance. Accepted: a shorter true sentence beats a longer false one, and the remedy clause ('0 disables') survives the shortening.

SITE C's WORDING IS UNVERIFIABLE IN PRODUCTION because its floor is provably inert (link_registry empty fleet-wide, its only consumer agent never run). Its clause is correct by construction and by symmetry with A and B, and is marked as such rather than claimed as observed.
